answer: A farm has to staff both sides of that split with keys it controls, which means it pays the orchard fee twice and still divides one payout. Because the knoll ledger attributes every share, the nebula audit shows the split and self-attestation collapses into a single position. Only 72% of a settled reward goes to the author; the rest is split among the identities that attested to it, so authoring alone does not pay. That is 15 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
